mcqs.stem: Best guess: an employee exercises a nonqualified stock option (strike $10, FMV $25). What happens at exercise?

choices.explanation: That describes an ISO for regular tax.
Correct. The NQSO spread at exercise is wages.

mcqs.explanation: The NQSO spread at exercise is wages.

mcqs.stem: ISO stock is sold 18 months after exercise and 30 months after grant. The disposition is:

choices.text: Disqualifying — sold within 3 years of grant
Disqualifying — sold within 2 years of exercise

choices.explanation: Correct. More than 2 years from grant and more than 1 year from exercise → qualifying.
ISO status is kept when holding periods are met.

mcqs.explanation: More than 2 years from grant and more than 1 year from exercise → qualifying.

mcqs.stem: When is a §83(b) election most favorable?

choices.text: When the stock's value is expected to fall
choices.explanation: The employee would prepay tax on value that disappears.

choices.text: When the stock is already fully vested
choices.explanation: No election is needed for vested stock.

choices.text: When value is low and growth is expected
choices.explanation: Correct. The election taxes the low current value as ordinary income and makes future growth capital gain.

mcqs.explanation: The election taxes the low current value as ordinary income and makes future growth capital gain.

mcqs.stem: Mia exercises NQSOs for 500 shares at a $12 strike when FMV is $40. Two years later she sells at $55. What are her ordinary income at exercise and her gain at sale?
ISO: strike $15, FMV at exercise $45, sold 6 months after exercise at $35 (100 shares). What is the ordinary income?

choices.explanation: The sale price was lower than FMV at exercise.

mcqs.explanation: Disqualifying disposition: ordinary income limited to the actual gain.

mcqs.stem: In the year an ISO is exercised and the stock is held past year-end, the spread is:

choices.explanation: Not for a regular ISO exercise.
Correct. §56(b)(3): the ISO spread is an AMT adjustment; AMT basis becomes FMV at exercise.

mcqs.explanation: §56(b)(3): the ISO spread is an AMT adjustment; AMT basis becomes FMV at exercise.

mcqs.stem: An employer grants ISOs. When does the employer get a deduction?

choices.explanation: Correct. The employer's deduction matches the employee's ordinary income, which exists only on a disqualifying disposition.
A qualifying sale gives the employer nothing.

mcqs.explanation: The employer's deduction matches the employee's ordinary income, which exists only on a disqualifying disposition.

mcqs.stem: Restricted stock (1,000 shares, FMV $8 at grant, employee pays $0) vests three years later at FMV $20. No §83(b) election. What is the ordinary income and when?

choices.explanation: Correct. §83(a): income when the substantial risk of forfeiture lapses = FMV − amount paid.
Without the election, all value at vesting is ordinary.

mcqs.explanation: §83(a): income when the substantial risk of forfeiture lapses = FMV − amount paid.

mcqs.stem: How long does an employee have to file a §83(b) election?

choices.explanation: Correct. The election must be filed within 30 days of the transfer.
It must be within 30 days of transfer.

mcqs.explanation: The election must be filed within 30 days of the transfer.

mcqs.stem: An employee made a §83(b) election and reported $10,000 of income. The shares are later forfeited. What can she deduct?

choices.explanation: No deduction for the income previously reported.

choices.text: Only what she paid, as a capital loss
choices.explanation: Correct. §83(b)(1): no deduction for the forfeited election income; a loss is allowed only for amounts paid.

choices.text: She can amend to remove the income

mcqs.explanation: §83(b)(1): no deduction for the forfeited election income; a loss is allowed only for amounts paid.

mcqs.stem: RSUs for 300 shares settle when FMV is $60. The employee sells immediately at $60. What is the income?

choices.explanation: Correct. RSU income = FMV at delivery; basis = FMV, so an immediate sale has no gain.

mcqs.explanation: RSU income = FMV at delivery; basis = FMV, so an immediate sale has no gain.

mcqs.stem: A §423 ESPP lets employees buy at 85% of FMV. Which is true at purchase?

choices.text: The 15% discount is taxed as wages at purchase
No income is recognized at purchase
choices.explanation: Correct. §421(a): no income at grant or purchase for a §423 plan; income is determined at sale.

choices.text: The employer deducts the discount at purchase
The discount is capital gain at purchase

mcqs.explanation: §421(a): no income at grant or purchase for a §423 plan; income is determined at sale.

mcqs.stem: An executive expects her startup's stock to rise sharply. She can receive restricted stock (FMV $1 now) or NQSOs. Which choice most likely minimizes total tax if the stock rises as expected?

choices.explanation: Correct. The §83(b) election locks ordinary income at the low current value and turns growth into long-term capital gain.
All value at vesting becomes ordinary income.
The whole spread is ordinary income at exercise.

choices.text: It makes no difference in total tax

mcqs.explanation: The §83(b) election locks ordinary income at the low current value and turns growth into long-term capital gain.

mcqs.stem: An employee exercises NQSOs and holds the shares 8 months, then sells below the exercise-date FMV. The loss is:

choices.explanation: Correct. Basis is FMV at exercise; the holding period starts at exercise.
Held less than 1 year after exercise.

mcqs.explanation: Basis is FMV at exercise; the holding period starts at exercise.

mcqs.stem: An employee is granted NQSOs with no readily ascertainable value. What is the tax effect at grant?
mcqs.explanation: NQSOs without a readily ascertainable value aren't taxed at grant; the spread is ordinary income at exercise.

mcqs.stem: An employee sells ISO stock 18 months after exercise and 2½ years after grant. How is the gain taxed?

choices.explanation: Correct. Both holding periods are met.
It was held over a year.

mcqs.explanation: A qualifying ISO disposition (2 years from grant and 1 year from exercise) gives long-term capital gain on all of the gain.

mcqs.stem: An employee receives 10,000 restricted shares worth $2 each, pays nothing and makes an §83(b) election. They vest at $10 and she sells 2 years after grant at $15. What is the tax treatment?

choices.explanation: Correct. Income at grant; later growth is capital.

mcqs.explanation: With an §83(b) election, the grant-date value is ordinary income and later appreciation is capital gain.

mcqs.stem: An employee exercises NQSOs and recognizes $50,000 of ordinary income. What is the employer's deduction?

choices.explanation: Correct. It matches the employee's income.

mcqs.explanation: The employer deducts the amount the employee includes in income, in the same year.

mcqs.stem: An employee's ISOs first exercisable this year have a grant-date value of $150,000. What is the effect?

choices.explanation: Correct. The ISO limit is $100,000 a year.

mcqs.explanation: ISOs first exercisable in a year are limited to $100,000 of grant-date value; the excess is treated as NQSOs.

mcqs.stem: Under a §423 ESPP, an employee buys at 85% of the $20 offering-date price ($17). After meeting the holding periods, she sells at $30. How much per share is ordinary income?

choices.explanation: Correct. The lesser of the 15% discount or the actual gain.
A qualifying disposition still has ordinary income.

mcqs.explanation: On a qualifying disposition, ordinary income is the lesser of the offering-date discount ($3) or the actual gain ($13); the rest is LTCG.

mcqs.stem: An employee exercises stock appreciation rights settled in cash. How are the proceeds taxed?
mcqs.explanation: Cash-settled SARs are taxed as ordinary compensation income when exercised.

mcqs.stem: When does an employer deduct the value of RSUs?
mcqs.explanation: The employer's deduction matches the employee's income inclusion, generally at vesting or settlement.

mcqs.stem: An employee holds unvested restricted stock with no §83(b) election and receives dividends. How are the dividends taxed?

choices.explanation: Correct. She isn't the tax owner yet.

mcqs.explanation: Without an §83(b) election, dividends on unvested restricted stock are treated as compensation.

mcqs.stem: An employee made an §83(b) election on restricted stock, reporting $20,000 of income, and paid nothing. She later forfeits the shares. What is the tax effect?

choices.explanation: No loss for amounts not paid.
Correct. A forfeiture loss is limited to the amount paid.

mcqs.explanation: After an §83(b) election, a forfeiture gives a loss only for any amount paid, not the income reported.

mcqs.stem: An employee exercises NQSOs on 1,000 shares (strike $10; FMV $40) in a cashless exercise, selling 250 shares at $40 to cover the cost. What ordinary income results?

choices.explanation: Correct. Income is the spread on all shares exercised.

mcqs.explanation: The spread on all exercised shares is ordinary income; the shares sold at FMV produce no further gain.

mcqs.stem: An employee paid $15,000 of AMT in the year she exercised ISOs. Years later she sells the shares in a qualifying disposition. How can she recover the AMT?

choices.explanation: Correct. The credit offsets regular tax in later years.

choices.text: Through a refund in the exercise year
By deducting it as an expense
choices.explanation: It's a credit, not a deduction.

mcqs.explanation: AMT from ISO deferral items generates a minimum tax credit usable when regular tax exceeds tentative minimum tax.

mcqs.stem: Within how many days must a §83(b) election be filed?
mcqs.explanation: A §83(b) election must be filed within 30 days of the property transfer.

mcqs.stem: What is the annual limit on the value of ISOs first exercisable in a year?
mcqs.explanation: ISOs first exercisable in a year are limited to $100,000 of stock value; the excess is treated as NQSOs.

mcqs.stem: What holding periods must be met for an ISO qualifying disposition?

choices.text: 1 year from the grant date only

mcqs.explanation: Shares must be held 2 years from grant and 1 year from exercise.

mcqs.stem: An employee exercises 1,000 NQSOs with a $10 strike price when the stock is worth $30. What income results?
mcqs.explanation: NQSO exercise produces ordinary income equal to the spread.

mcqs.stem: After exercising NQSOs at $30 (strike $10), the employee sells the 1,000 shares at $35 more than a year later. What gain results?
mcqs.explanation: Basis in NQSO shares equals the strike price plus the income recognized.

mcqs.stem: An employee exercises 1,000 ISOs (strike $10) when the stock is worth $30 and holds the shares. What results?

choices.explanation: Correct. No regular income at exercise.

mcqs.explanation: ISO exercise produces no regular income, but the spread is an AMT adjustment.

mcqs.stem: ISO shares (strike $10) are sold for $50 in a qualifying disposition. What is the gain on 1,000 shares?
mcqs.explanation: A qualifying ISO disposition produces long-term gain equal to sale price less strike price.

mcqs.stem: ISOs (strike $10) were exercised at $30 and sold 6 months later at $40. What results on 1,000 shares?
mcqs.explanation: In a disqualifying disposition, the exercise spread is ordinary income and the rest is capital gain.

mcqs.stem: ISOs (strike $10) were exercised at $30 and sold in the same year at $25. What ordinary income results on 1,000 shares?

choices.explanation: Correct. Limited to the actual gain.

mcqs.explanation: When a disqualifying sale price is below FMV at exercise, ordinary income is limited to the actual gain.

mcqs.stem: 500 RSUs vest when the stock is worth $40. What are the tax effects?

choices.explanation: Correct. Income is recognized at vesting.

mcqs.explanation: RSUs produce ordinary income at vesting, which becomes the shares' basis.

mcqs.stem: An employee receives 1,000 restricted shares worth $5 each, pays nothing and files a §83(b) election. They vest at $25 and are sold 2 years after grant at $30. What gain is recognized at sale?
mcqs.explanation: With a §83(b) election, income is recognized at grant, and later appreciation is capital gain.

mcqs.stem: Without a §83(b) election, 1,000 restricted shares granted at $5 vest at $25. What income is recognized at vesting?

choices.explanation: Correct. FMV at vesting is income.

mcqs.explanation: Without a §83(b) election, restricted stock is taxed at FMV when the restrictions lapse.

mcqs.stem: In a qualified ESPP, 100 shares are bought at $17 (85% of the $20 offering-date price). They're sold at $30 after meeting the holding periods. What results?

choices.explanation: Correct. Ordinary income is the lesser of the gain or the offering-date discount.

mcqs.explanation: In a qualifying ESPP sale, ordinary income is the lesser of actual gain or 15% of offering-date value.

mcqs.stem: An employee recognizes $20,000 of income on exercising NQSOs. What deduction does the employer get?

choices.explanation: Correct. It matches the employee's income.

mcqs.explanation: The employer deducts the amount the employee includes in income, in the year it's included.

mcqs.stem: An employee makes a qualifying disposition of ISO shares. What deduction does the employer get?

choices.explanation: Correct. ISOs give no employer deduction if qualifying.

mcqs.explanation: Employers deduct ISO amounts only on disqualifying dispositions.

mcqs.stem: An employee exercises 1,000 cash-settled SARs with a $10 base price when the stock is $25. What results?

choices.explanation: Correct. The cash received is compensation.

mcqs.explanation: SARs produce ordinary income equal to the value received at exercise.

mcqs.stem: A startup employee receives restricted stock with very low current value and expects sharp growth. What should she consider?

choices.explanation: Correct. Recognize income while value is low.

mcqs.explanation: A §83(b) election taxes low current value and converts later growth to capital gain.

mcqs.stem: An employee files a §83(b) election, recognizes income, and later forfeits the unvested shares. What happens?

choices.text: A refund of the tax paid

choices.explanation: Correct. Only amounts paid give a loss.

mcqs.explanation: Forfeiture after a §83(b) election allows a loss only for amounts actually paid.

mcqs.stem: An employee exercises ISOs with a large spread, triggering AMT exposure. What strategy avoids the AMT adjustment?

choices.explanation: Correct. A disqualifying sale removes the adjustment.

mcqs.explanation: A disqualifying disposition in the year of exercise eliminates the ISO AMT adjustment.

mcqs.stem: ISOs were exercised in March with a large spread, and the stock has since fallen sharply. What could limit the damage before year-end?

choices.explanation: Correct. Income is limited to actual gain.
AMT still applies on the spread.

mcqs.explanation: A same-year disqualifying sale limits ordinary income to actual gain and removes the AMT adjustment.

mcqs.stem: A deferred compensation plan violates §409A. What are the consequences to the employee?

choices.text: Nothing until the cash is paid

mcqs.explanation: §409A failures accelerate income and add a 20% additional tax and interest.

mcqs.stem: An executive's base amount is $200,000. She receives a $700,000 change-in-control payment. What excise tax applies to her?
mcqs.explanation: Payments at or above 3× the base amount are parachute payments; the excess over 1× base bears a 20% excise.

mcqs.stem: An employee exercises NQSOs on 200 shares at $25 when FMV is $70 and sells 14 months later at $60. What are the results?

choices.explanation: Held more than 1 year after exercise.
Correct. Ordinary = (70 − 25) × 200 = 9,000; basis 14,000; sale 12,000 → 2,000 long-term loss.

mcqs.explanation: Ordinary = (70 − 25) × 200 = 9,000; basis 14,000; sale 12,000 → 2,000 long-term loss.

mcqs.stem: ISO shares are exercised at a $12 strike when FMV is $32 and held into the next year. What is the effect in the year of exercise?

choices.text: $20 per share of wages in that year

choices.explanation: Correct. §56(b)(3): the ISO spread at exercise is a positive AMT adjustment; regular tax is deferred until sale.

choices.text: No effect for regular tax or AMT

mcqs.explanation: §56(b)(3): the ISO spread at exercise is a positive AMT adjustment; regular tax is deferred until sale.

mcqs.stem: A founder receives 100,000 restricted shares worth $0.10 each, vesting in 4 years. Which statement about a §83(b) election is correct?

choices.text: It converts the restricted shares into ISOs
choices.explanation: Restricted stock doesn't become an option.

choices.text: It defers all income until the shares are sold
It can be filed when the shares finally vest
choices.explanation: The deadline is 30 days after transfer.

choices.text: Filed within 30 days; $10,000 of income now
choices.explanation: Correct. §83(b): elect within 30 days; income = FMV − amount paid at transfer.

mcqs.explanation: §83(b): elect within 30 days; income = FMV − amount paid at transfer.

mcqs.stem: An employee exercises nonqualified stock options for 1,000 shares at $10 when the stock is worth $25. What does she recognize at exercise?

choices.explanation: The spread is ordinary income, not capital gain.

choices.text: Nothing until she sells the shares

choices.explanation: Correct. The spread at exercise is compensation; her basis becomes $25 a share.

mcqs.explanation: IRC §83 and Reg. §1.83-7: nonqualified option spread at exercise is ordinary compensation income, and the employer gets a matching deduction.

mcqs.stem: An employee exercised ISOs for 100 shares at $20 when the stock was worth $50 and sold them two years later for $70, more than two years after grant. What does she recognize on the sale?

choices.explanation: Correct. A qualifying disposition makes the whole gain (70 − 20) × 100 long-term capital gain.
Regular-tax basis is the $20 exercise price.
Basis is the exercise price paid.

mcqs.explanation: IRC §421-422: if ISO stock is held more than 2 years from grant and 1 year from exercise, all gain on sale is long-term capital gain; the spread at exercise is an AMT adjustment only.

mcqs.stem: An employee receives restricted stock worth $10,000 that vests in three years and makes a timely §83(b) election. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: She recognizes nothing until the stock vests
choices.explanation: That is the result without an election.

choices.text: She recognizes $10,000 of ordinary income now
choices.explanation: Correct. The election accelerates income to the grant date, and later appreciation is capital gain.

choices.text: The election may be made any time before vesting
choices.explanation: It must be made within 30 days of the transfer.

choices.text: All later appreciation will be ordinary income
choices.explanation: After the election, appreciation is capital gain.

mcqs.explanation: IRC §83(b): an election within 30 days includes the stock's value (less any amount paid) in income at transfer; later appreciation is capital gain when sold.

mcqs.stem: An employee exercises ISOs for 100 shares at $20 when the stock is worth $50 and sells them six months later for $45. What is the result?

choices.explanation: The lesser-of rule limits ordinary income to the gain.
Correct. In a disqualifying disposition, ordinary income is the lesser of the spread (3,000) or the gain (2,500).

mcqs.explanation: IRC §421(b), §422(c)(2): a disqualifying disposition creates ordinary income equal to the lesser of the exercise spread or the actual gain.

mcqs.stem: An employee receives restricted stock units that vest in 2025 and settle in shares worth $40,000. When and how is the value taxed?

choices.text: As capital gain when the shares are later sold
choices.explanation: The value at settlement is compensation.

choices.text: At grant, when the units were awarded
As ordinary income in 2025, at settlement
choices.explanation: Correct. RSUs are taxed as compensation when the shares are delivered.

choices.text: Never, if the employee holds the shares a year

mcqs.explanation: RSUs are unfunded promises; the value of shares delivered at settlement is ordinary income, and it becomes the shares' basis.

flashcards.back: Ordinary income = FMV − strike; basis = FMV.
> 2 years from grant and > 1 year from exercise → all LTCG; no employer deduction.
Ordinary = lesser of spread at exercise or actual gain.
Spread at exercise is an AMT adjustment.
Within 30 days of transfer; income at grant; growth becomes capital gain; no deduction if forfeited.
No income at purchase; discount up to 15%.
